dataSheet.description: A generic rear-wheel-drive two-seat sports car in the 1.35 t class: roughly 175 kW, 2.5 m wheelbase, 48/52 front/rear weight distribution, wider rear tires, with ABS, traction and stability control on by default.
sources: Class-typical figures from manufacturer specification sheets for front-engine RWD sports cars (mass 1300–1450 kg, wheelbase 2.45–2.55 m, Cd 0.28–0.32, 48–52 % on the front axle).

Tire feel parameters tuned to a ~1.0 g skidpad and ~34 m 100–0 km/h braking distance from published road tests for the class; the rear tire is a wider staggered fitment with more grip and cornering stiffness than the front, so the car settles into mild understeer rather than near-neutral handling.
Suspension rates typical of a sports car with ~2.0 Hz front and ~2.2 Hz rear ride frequencies and a front-biased roll stiffness distribution (Milliken & Milliken, Race Car Vehicle Dynamics, ch. 16).

Drivetrain [ILLUSTRATIVE]: a 3.5 l naturally aspirated six (peak 405 N·m at 5000 rpm, about 250 kW at 7000 rpm), six-speed ratios with a 3.6 final drive and a mild clutch-pack LSD at the low end of the class's drive bias range (Milliken & Milliken, Race Car Vehicle Dynamics, ch. 20).
Steering geometry [ILLUSTRATIVE]: 7° caster (about 30 mm of trail), 12 mm scrub radius and a light assist, for the heavier, more communicative steering of a sports car.

Roll centres [ILLUSTRATIVE]: double-wishbone front near 50 mm and multilink rear near 100 mm (Milliken & Milliken ch. 17); a small rear spoiler leaves a touch of rear downforce and near-zero front lift (Hucho ch. 4).

Travel curves [ILLUSTRATIVE] (ADR-0026): roll-centre height falling with bump and camber gain at rates scaled from the curves derived for Project Chrono's BMW E90 from its hardpoints (MacPherson front: roll centre −2.9 mm per mm of bump, camber about −20°/m; double wishbone: −1.6 mm per mm; docs/validation/chrono-bmw-e90.md), eased for this car's lower roll centres. No toe curves: road cars are set up for near-zero bump steer, and the E90 comparison found toe follows force more than travel.
dataSheet.notes: Not a specific production model. The rear differential is a clutch-pack limited slip (preload 20 N·m, 1.6:1 drive, 1.2:1 coast). ABS, traction control and stability control are on at the core's default settings; turn them off in `assists` for an unassisted car.
